text:
Seoul shares opened higher Thursday ahead of the stock market debut of U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic PBC this week amid concerns over the sustainability of AI investments.
After opening 0.45 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) rose 6.39 points, or 0.13 percent, to 5,073.83 as of 9:15 a.m.
The index ended 1.99 percent higher at 5,067.44 on Wednesday, snapping a four-day losing streak, buoyed by a rally in technology stocks following Nvidia Corp.'s upbeat earnings.
Overnight, U.S. stocks closed mixed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.11 percent, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite rose 0.42 percent.
Investors are looking for further evidence that heavy investments in AI will generate sustainable returns as Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI chatbot, is set to make its stock market debut Thursday (U.S. time).
Tourism agency Hana Tour surged 17.07 percent, while national flag carrier Korean Air gained 2.72 percent and low-cost carrier Jeju Air jumped 13.07 percent.
Tourism-related stocks advanced after Korea and China reached a substantive conclusion to negotiations on services and investment under their bilateral free trade agreement (FTA), paving the way for greater access to the Chinese market for South Korean films, games and other businesses.
Among decliners, market bellwether Samsung Electronics fell 1.13 percent and its chipmaking rival SK hynix declined 0.96 percent.
The Korean won was quoted at 1,330.75 won against the U.S. dollar as of 9:15 a.m., up 2.95 won from the previous trading session's close.
